name: Nigeria

findings.summary: MTN Nigeria launched commercial 5G in selected Lagos and other areas on an Ericsson-supplied 5G radio access network and non-standalone packet core, extending a roughly 21-year Ericsson-MTN Nigeria partnership.
findings.analyst_inference: Ericsson is Swedish, so pole third under the equipment rule. Tier 5 reflects a live commercial launch, though only a first-phase footprint. Neither source mentions Huawei; MTN Nigeria's 2G-4G vendor mix and Airtel/Globacom 5G suppliers were not established in this pass. Contract value not disclosed.

findings.summary: Galaxy Backbone and Huawei agreed in 2018 to build phase II of the national ICT backbone (NICTIB II), fibre to 19 northern states, on a US$328m China Exim credit; federal approval followed in July 2020.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: Huawei as equipment vendor/contractor per the 2018 agreement (ThisDay, Techpoint); Techpoint notes the contractor was not formally confirmed. Tier 2 because only the MoU and government approval are evidenced; loan closing, construction and completion were not found. Capacity Media supports the loan but does not name Huawei.

findings.local_actor: Kasi Cloud LOS1 campus, Lekki, Lagos; Nigeria Sovereign Investment Authority (foundational investor)
findings.summary: Kasi Cloud launched its LOS1 AI-oriented data-centre campus in Lekki, Lagos in May 2026, moving into commissioning; it is designed to scale to about 100 MW, with the sovereign wealth fund NSIA as a foundational investor.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic: owner-operator is a Nigerian company backed by NSIA; full shareholding not disclosed. Tier 4 (built, commissioning) rather than 5, as operation at scale is not evidenced. The US$250m value is from TechCabal only. Chip vendor and builder not stated.

findings.summary: Airtel Nigeria plans a 38 MW, 3,000-plus-rack hyperscale data centre in Eko Atlantic, Lagos, under its Nxtra brand, costing over US$120m and pitched at GPU-powered AI workloads; completion was targeted for Q1 2026.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole third: Airtel Africa is London-listed and controlled by India's Bharti Airtel. Tier 1 as Developing Telecoms reports a plan; TechCabal (Jan 2026) says early GPU shipments arrived in late 2025, implying construction, but this rests on one S3 source. Go-live and GPU vendor unconfirmed.

findings.summary: Cassava Technologies' Nvidia-powered AI factory rollout, which began in South Africa, is slated to expand to Nigeria, Kenya, Egypt and Morocco; no Nigerian GPU count, value or timetable was given.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule: Nvidia is the controller, so pole us. Tier 1: Nigeria named only as a planned expansion site. The pan-African programme was reported at US$700m, not apportioned to Nigeria.

findings.controller: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy / NCAIR with Awarri Technologies
findings.local_actor: Awarri Technologies; National Centre for Artificial Intelligence and Robotics
findings.summary: Nigeria's government unveiled N-ATLAS at UNGA80, an open multilingual model for Yoruba, Hausa, Igbo and Nigerian-accented English built with Awarri and NCAIR; free for research, with commercial deployments above 1,000 users needing a licence.

sources.publisher: Federal Ministry of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy

findings.analyst_inference: Pole domestic: released by the Nigerian government with a Nigerian partner; exact weights holder not stated but the licence terms imply national control. Base model Llama-3 8B (Meta, us) per Open Source For You only; speech component reportedly fine-tuned from Whisper Small (OpenAI). Tier 5 reflects release, not proven adoption.

findings.local_actor: Federal Government of Nigeria (National Public Security Communications System); Abuja, Lagos and other cities
findings.summary: ZTE was contracted for the roughly US$470m National Public Security Communications System, including CCTV in Abuja and other cities, on a China Exim loan; lawmakers in 2025 called it failed and abandoned while repayments continue.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc (equipment vendor ZTE). Award reported as 2008 with the MoU/loan in 2010; date set to 2010. still_current false based on October 2025 House of Representatives characterisation; Blueprint reports a post-2019 revival via an Indian concessionaire (NPS Technology), not verified. Not coded as a reversal: failure appears operational/procurement-related, not geopolitical. No S1/S2 source opened.

power.null_reason: no AI/data-centre-specific power evidence surfaced; budget spent on other layers

research_gaps: Was the NICTIB II China Exim loan closed and the Huawei-built northern fibre backbone constructed or completed?
Radio and core vendors for Airtel Nigeria, Globacom and 9mobile, and MTN Nigeria's legacy 2G-4G mix (Huawei/ZTE share).
Status of the ZTE National Public Security Communications System contract, the Indian NPS Technology concession, and the 2025 House probe outcome.
Did Airtel/Nxtra's Eko Atlantic facility go live, and with which GPU vendor? Kasi Cloud LOS1 tenants and chip vendor.
Any Nigerian government adoption of OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, Anthropic or PRC model services; Google AI fund grants were seen but not coded as stack adoption.
Who holds the N-ATLAS weights (Awarri vs NCAIR/ministry) and is the Llama-3 8B base confirmed by a primary source (e.g. the model card)?
